note: Both give the full Leontius passage, marginalia and apparatus; the only difference is breathing on 'αὐτὸν/αὑτὸν' in the last line.

Y matches the print with 'ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας', 'μὲν οὖν καὶ σημεῖα' and margin 'Bl. vigintiquinque drachm.', where X has 'ὑπὸ τοῖς ποσὶν', omits 'καὶ' and reads 'id est'; neither error changes the sense much.
Same text and apparatus; X adds a stray '»' before 'Ἰωάννης' and Y misreads 'ν ausradiert' as 'υ ausradiert', both trivial.
Both give the standard Iliad 1.1-17 text; X also keeps the interlinear marginal gloss ('ἄγως ἔδωκεν') beside line 4, which Y drops.

X roughly follows the hand ('ἐξ ὄρους φαράν', 'ἀστερ … ὄντος· ἄλλως'), but Y invents a long marginal block and different running text ('καὶ τὰ καθ᾽ ἑρμηνείαν', 'ἀστερίσκος ὕμνος') that is not on the leaf.
Both texts are the same as the print; the only differences are apparatus trivia ('διτῶν' vs 'δίϊτον' for printed 'διϖον').
Same Greek text, marginalia and apparatus line '23. καὶ τοῖς Α²ΠΜ : τοῖς Α.'; only the placement of tags differs.
X reads 'οὐκ εἰκότως μυρμιδόνα εἶπε', which reverses the printed 'ὃν εἰκότως'; X also has 'διεσαφήσειεν', 'δεδομένον' and 'θηβαίου' where the print and Y have 'διεσάφησεν', 'δεδεμένον' and 'θυβαίου'.
Both reproduce the opening of Republic X, its marginalia and the note '7. παραδεκτέα ΑΠ : παραδεκτέον Α²Μ.' with no substantive differences.
Y keeps the printed abbreviation 'GEB.' and correctly describes the owl on an open book; X expands to 'GEBORENE' and says 'two closed books', which is minor either way.
